questions.prompt: Tell me about your snack yesterday in one short sentence. Was it an apple, an orange, or an egg?
questions.context: Small talk about food at home yesterday

questions.prompt: Morning things: what do you carry or use before you leave home? Say one short sentence about an umbrella, an alarm, or an iced coffee.
You have one hour free after work today. Say in one or two short sentences what you want to do in an hour like that.
At the office today, what small thing did you write or send? Tell me in a short sentence about an email or an answer to your team.
questions.context: Light work talk about today's office tasks

questions.prompt: Your team needs one new idea for next week. Say your own idea in one short sentence — start with 'I have...' or 'I want to share...'.
questions.context: Sharing an idea with a teammate

reason: 짧은 문장에서도 'a/an'을 자주 빠뜨리고, 'an'을 'a'처럼 발음하고 있어서 오늘은 이 두 가지를 함께 연습해요.

instruction.sentence_length: short single-clause sentences; allow a second short clause only when the learner sounds ready
instruction.hint_timing: wait for one full attempt, then hint after a short pause or a second try
contexts: sharing an idea with a teammate

level.reason: 기본 단문은 만들 수 있지만 관사와 발음이 아직 불안정해서 A2에서 더 다지는 것이 좋습니다.

notes: Articles appear when the sentence is very short and familiar ('I had a meeting yesterday') but disappear with longer noun phrases ('was project architecture meeting').
Learner self-corrects when given a second try, so short waiting time before hints works well.
Speaks in fragments and finishes the sentence in a second turn; encourage one complete sentence per turn.
Recent Korean-script attempts suggest reading aloud is hard; prompts asking for own content work better.
